body: @jstenback Could I please get an invite to tomorrow's meeting? Email is stephanie.zhang@microsoft.com. Thanks!
I had a question for https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12339 that came up - how do we feel about adding `shadowRootAdoptedStyleSheets` attribute on `HTMLTemplateElement` for feature detection?
I'll include that in the agenda. Also, apologies for getting the time of tomorrow's meeting incorrect, it's at 9am PDT, AMER-EMEA friendly time.

Minutes:

- Carryover Issue 11542 (Stage 3 Request): The discussion of issue 11542, concerning a stage three request for patching, was brief and was determined not to have the necessary quorum to proceed. This issue will be held off until the next meeting, and Johnny Stenback noted an error in scheduling the time of the current meeting.
- Issue 12388 Stage Advancement (Spellcheck API): The group agreed to move the Spellcheck API proposal to stage one, as there were no fundamental objections. Brian Kardell noted that they were addressing comments regarding the limitations of the current proposal and the potential for a more flexible, regular-expression-like approach. Keith Cirkel requested that the reasoning for using a bespoke API (add and delete) instead of a set-like interface (has) be included in the explainer, as the words themselves should not be detectable in the spellcheck.
- Issue 12309 (Document Picture-in-Picture): The topic of upstreaming the document picture-in-picture implementation into the HTML specification was raised. It was noted that the necessary people who could discuss the pushback on this proposal were not present, so the issue will be carried over to the next meeting.
- Issue 11542 (Out-of-Order HTML Streaming): The issue related to out-of-order HTML streaming and patching was kept on the agenda because it is currently blocked awaiting review from Mozilla. Noam Rosenthal stated they had been holding the agenda status until Mozilla looked at the request for stage three.
- Issue 11478 (Opaque Range Interface) Stage 3 Proposal: Stephanie Zhang proposed advancing the opaque range interface proposal to stage three, citing that the proposal is in good shape and Chromium is starting the shipping process. Keith Cirkel questioned if the specification text was truly "complete" given some outstanding review notes, particularly one from Simon regarding the timing of updating opaque ranges relative to the input event. Stephanie Zhang agreed to research the timing issue further since the behavior of this new range type is unprecedented.
- Opaque Range Stage Advancement Decision: Luke noted that support from at least two implementers is required for advancement, and WebKit's position is tending positive. The decision on advancing the opaque range interface to stage three was postponed for one week to allow Stephanie Zhang to address the timing concerns.
- Issue 10378 (Video Poster Image Responsive Images/Alt Text): Discussion on enabling responsive images and alt text for the HTML video poster image was deferred because the relevant people from Squarespace were not present. Johnny Stenback decided to remove the agenda plus label and requested that the issue be added back when they are ready to return to the meeting to discuss it.
- PR 12339 (Shadow Root Adopted Stylesheets): Kurt Catti-Schmidt raised an issue regarding feature detection for the `shadowrootadoptedstylesheets` attribute on the template tag for declarative shadow DOM. It was determined that the attribute should have an IDL (Interface Definition Language) reflection on the `HTMLTemplateElement.prototype` for feature detection, even though the reflection would not be live and would be primarily for detecting the feature.
- PR 12339 Stage Advancement and Review: The feature associated with PR 12339 was requested to be moved from stage one to stage two, as the pull requests were open and the feature shape was established. Keith Cirkel and Johnny Stenback updated the issue status to stage two, and Kurt Catti-Schmidt committed to updating the spec text and moving toward stage three in the coming weeks. Luke pointed out that the IDL attribute may need a manual algorithm for reflection due to the use of URLs, which DOM token lists do not typically handle.
- PR 12339 Discussion on Imperative Symmetry: There was a discussion about adding an imperative counterpart to the declarative `shadowrootadoptedstylesheets` within the `attachShadow` method for symmetry, particularly because the declarative version handles loading URLs. Kurt Catti-Schmidt acknowledged the symmetry point but indicated that the existing imperative API for adopted stylesheets might be preferred, and they would consider it further.
- PR 12069 (Select Multiple Drop Down Base Appearance): Joey Arhar confirmed that they had addressed the reviews from Simon and Anna on this PR. Luke suggested blocking the PR until a separate spec issue regarding how the selected option works is resolved, as they believe authors will immediately try to use that functionality.
- PR 12069 (Select Multiple Drop Down Base Appearance) Status: Joey Arhar agreed with the suggestion to resolve the associated selected option spec issue before merging the PR. The plan is to continue working on that spec issue, potentially combining the changes, and they agreed to keep this item on the agenda for the next meeting.
- PR 11454 (Sticky Activation): Mustaq Ahmed provided an update on the sticky activation pull request, confirming consensus that sticky activation should carry over after a same-origin navigation. They noted that Chrome's behavior differs from general expectations regarding navigation from A to B to A (where B redirects back to A), but a test has been added to match the general expected behavior, unblocking the pull request. Luke indicated the PR needs to be finalized and editorially reviewed to allow WebKit to implement it.
